result.title: Keeping LLM Agents on Procedure: Executable Finite-State Control for Long-Horizon Instruction Fidelity
result.summary: Much of the automation handed to language-model agents is procedural: each step needs little intelligence, but a long unattended run must follow a skill or SOP stated once at the start. We show that agents drift from such procedures over long runs, and that restating the instructions or resuming a stopped agent only moves the drift to another shortcut. We study an executable finite-state machine (FSM) that keeps the workflow state outside the model's context and enforces it at three points: tool calls, state transitions and the end of the agent's turn. In a pre-registered experiment on 200-account SOP-Bench batches, Claude Haiku 4.5 with the FSM decided on average 139 accounts correctly and by the procedure, against 48 for the strongest baseline (95% CI of the difference [46, 130]), and kept this rate to the end; across three models, the gain tracked how much the plain agent drifted. Because the runtime, not the model, supplies this long-horizon reliability, the FSM can let small models carry procedural work: Haiku 4.5 with it averaged more such decisions than plain Claude Sonnet 4.6 at 38% of the cost. Analyses on SWE-bench Verified, $τ^2$-bench, and staged and cross-context workflows further suggest that reliable long-horizon automation can come from stronger execution control, not only stronger models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出 LLM agent 在长程流程化任务中会偏离初始 SOP，重述指令或恢复中断只能把漂移搬家；作者提出把工作流状态放在模型上下文之外的可执行有限状态机，在工具调用、状态转移和轮次结束时强制约束，并在 SOP-Bench 等基准上验证长程可靠性提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉或多模态 latent reasoning 无直接关系，但「外部显式状态机 vs 模型内部隐式状态」的对照可为 latent 状态的维持、漂移诊断与停止决策提供问题表述上的启发，具体可迁移性有待核查。
